title: WILKINSON 1907 PATTERN BAYONET
identification: British Pattern 1907 sword bayonet with scabbard, wood grips, dated '10 FEB'15' with crown over 1907 on one ricasso face. Other face has 18, R, X (bend test) and Japanese-looking characters. Wilkinson name not seen in photos 5 and 6. Guard looks without hooked quillon (hook was dropped in 1915). Japanese-like marks not explained by anything found; sources say P1907 was modelled on the Japanese Type 30 but no Japanese-contract P1907 was confirmed.

title: BOX OF 18TH CENTURY PORCELAIN - SOME DAMAGE
identification: Box of 6 to 8 pieces of 18th c English porcelain, mostly Worcester type c.1760-85. Photo 2 shows a fluted teabowl with blue open crescent mark (Worcester) and a pierced strainer dish with a blue pseudo-Chinese or fret-type mark, cracked and chipped (rim chip visible). Photo 3 shows a scale blue and gilt fluted teapot with polychrome flower sprays and floral lid, c.1770, Worcester style; no damage visible in photos but not inspected. Also a blue and white sauceboat, a blue and white mug with floral sprays, a blue and white cup, a small leaf-shaped dish and a cup with a painted insect inside. Some pieces could be Caughley or Lowestoft rather than Worcester; the scale blue teapot is the key piece, and may be Worcester or a good later copy (Samson or Chamberlain style) - needs checking.
chrome_hint: eBay sold: 'Worcester scale blue teapot 18th century' and 'Worcester fluted teabowl crescent mark' (Sold items); also LiveAuctioneers/Invaluable results for 'Worcester scale blue teapot fluted' and the-saleroom Worcester price guide.

title: BOX OF VINTAGE MILITARY RELATED BOOKS & 2 TASMANIAN YEAR BOOKS
identification: Box of about 22 green cloth Australian War Memorial wartime Christmas-style annuals plus two red cloth Tasmanian Year Book 1971 volumes. Readable spines: These Eagles, RAAF Log, HMAS (Mk IV), Stand Easy, On Guard, RAAF Saga, As You Were 1948, As You Were 1950. About 13 further green spines lie flat and cannot be read. Titles not readable: the flat spines and the volume between RAAF Log and Stand Easy. Single photo only. These annuals had very large print runs (Stand Easy 162,240 and RAAF Saga 95,730 by 1957 per AWM), so they are common; the first printings were free or cheap to servicemen.
